jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}最近[さいきん]、釣[つ]り{ばかり|bakari-only}しています。
en: Lately my older brother does nothing but fish.
why: ばかり after a noun means that one thing happens over and over to the exclusion of others.

jp: 今年[ことし]{の|no-possessive}冬[ふゆ]{は|wa-topic}、曇[くも]り{の|no-possessive}日[ひ]{ばかり|bakari-only}です。
en: This winter has been nothing but cloudy days.
why: 日ばかりです says the days are all of one kind; しか would need a negative.

jp: 父[ちち]{は|wa-topic}お酒[さけ]{ばかり|bakari-only}飲[の]んで、野菜[やさい]{を|o-object}食[た]べません。
en: My father drinks nothing but alcohol and does not eat vegetables.
why: お酒ばかり飲む means he keeps drinking alcohol and little else.

jp: うち{の|no-possessive}チーム{は|wa-topic}、最近[さいきん]負[ま]けて{ばかり|bakari-only}います。
en: Our team has been doing nothing but losing lately.
why: V-て+ばかりいる means doing the same thing all the time, here losing again and again.

jp: この森[もり]{は|wa-topic}大[おお]きな木[き]{ばかり|bakari-only}です。
en: This forest is nothing but big trees.
why: 木ばかりです says everything there is a big tree.

jp: 山[やま]{の|no-possessive}道[みち]{は|wa-topic}石[いし]{ばかり|bakari-only}で、歩[ある]きにくいです。
en: The mountain path is nothing but stones, so it is hard to walk on.
why: 石ばかりで says the path is full of stones and nothing else.

jp: 娘[むすめ]{は|wa-topic}ピアノ{の|no-possessive}練習[れんしゅう]{ばかり|bakari-only}して、友達[ともだち]{と|to-with}遊[あそ]びません。
en: My daughter does nothing but practice the piano and does not play with her friends.
why: 練習ばかりして means she does only practice, as the next clause confirms.
